purpose: Teacher-supplied classroom scope for question authoring and review
authoringRules: Retain typed definition-to-concept questions as requested.
Choice questions should rehearse audible recognition, musical features and knowledge directly supporting those features.
Use the relevant workbook to choose the taught scope, level, vocabulary and useful comparisons.
Historical context, construction details and dramatic purpose may explain a definition, but should not displace listening recognition as the question focus.
Do not infer a genre from one generic cue; use combinations and appropriate context.
Booklet content supplies classroom scope, not permission to copy an inaccurate or overgeneralised musical statement. Preserve musical accuracy and qualify tendencies.

source.supportingText:
Contemporary jazz (AH)  A broad term for modern jazz styles that extend earlier jazz language through advanced harmony, rhythmic experimentation and unusual tone colours.
•  Rhythmic experimentation, including cross-rhythms and changing time signatures.
•  Experimental instrumental effects, such as melodic instruments used percussively and harmonics.
•  Unconventional jazz instruments, including flugelhorn, flute and oboe.
•  Improvisation may be combined with complex written material and changing textures.

classroomExamples.application: Improvisation with advanced harmony, rhythmic experimentation, unusual timbres and changing textures.
